title: FHFA House Price Index — monthly index (August 2027 data), 9:00 a.m. ET — FOMC day one, inside the communications blackout
source: FHFA: two FHFA primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06 by this session, independently of the sweep that proposed this id. (1) fhfa.gov/data/hpi (HTTP 200, 89,663 bytes) -- its "2027 HPI Release Dates" table, tenth of twelve dated rows, reads "Tuesday, October 26 | Monthly Index | August 2027"; the four rows the same table marks "Quarterly Index (with Monthly Tables)" are February 23, May 25, August 31 and November 30, so this row is a MONTHLY edition by the publisher's own labelling rather than by inference. (2) The published 2026Q2 report (HTTP 200, 1,522,949 bytes, released 2026-08-25), whose "FHFA HPI Release Dates for 2027" appendix page carries the identical row directly beneath the statement "Public FHFA HPI(R) releases occur at 9AM ET and include a press release, tables, figures, and associated data" -- a published document rather than a second reading of the same web table, and the source of the 9:00 a.m. ET time. The PDF's 517 stream objects were located and 511 inflated in-session with node zlib, then text-extracted from the Tj/TJ operators; this runner has no pdftotext, openpyxl or numpy. Promoted estimate -> confirmed on the precedent construction-spending-2026-12-01, new-home-sales-2026-11-25, fhfa-hpi-2026-11-24, fhfa-hpi-2026-12-29, fhfa-hpi-2027-01-26, fhfa-hpi-2027-02-23, fhfa-hpi-2027-08-31 and fhfa-hpi-2027-09-28 set: the no-self-confirm limit binds the DISCOVERING sweep (consumer-confidence-2027-10-26), not this event's own independent second look. 2027-10-26 is the last Tuesday of October 2027 and a full NYSE session, consistent with the rule the other eleven rows follow. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: PROPOSED by the consumer-confidence-2027-10-26 initial-research sweep (2026-09-06) and researched the same day; the proposal file is now shadowed by this canonical one. Its three cautions all held: the pairing is an identity rather than a feature of this date, the August-2027 reference month carries no information about the October CB survey panel, and the 9:00-10:00 ET window was the open question. INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-06 (docs/research/events/fhfa-hpi-2027-10-26.md) ANSWERS THAT OPEN QUESTION -- THE ONE FIVE SIBLING LEDGERS EACH RECORDED AS UNREACHABLE. (1) THE CLEAN WINDOW EXISTS AND WAS MEASURED. Yahoo's hourly chart endpoint with includePrePost=true serves a 09:00 ET pre-market bar covering 09:00-09:30 -- after the FHFA release, before the cash open, and a full half hour before the Conference Board prints at 10:00. 730 sessions are served (2023-10-09 -> 2026-09-04), containing 34 FHFA release mornings. EVERY SIGNIFICANT READING IS IN THE QUIET DIRECTION AND NONE IS DIRECTIONAL: median |return| 3.70 bps vs 8.59 (p=0.0196, seed-stable 0.0185-0.0204), median range 30.78 bps vs 52.39 (p=0.0316), signed return DEAD NULL at p=0.6550. The 09:30-10:30 bar that contains the open and the CB print is quieter too (|return| p=0.0278, range p=0.0256, volume p=0.0119). So at the finest resolution this data layer can reach, an FHFA release morning is NARROWER than a comparable morning, with no tilt -- the opposite sign from "the print moves the tape." (2) AND THE HONEST LIMIT THAT STOPS IT BEING A RESULT. Within the intraday window release day equals last Tuesday 34 of 34 (35 last Tuesdays, 34 releases), so no window can separate the print from its calendar slot -- only a pre-2021 sample can, and the intraday data does not reach back that far. Against the tightest matched control, other late-month Tuesdays, the effect lands at p=0.1017 (|return|, seed-stable 0.0976-0.1032) and p=0.0753 (range) on n=13 -- a tendency, not a finding. Yahoo also serves ZERO pre-market volume on this endpoint (every one of the 34 bars reads 0), so the depth behind those bps is unknown and they are quote observations, not fills. (3) THE DATA BOUNDARY IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: 1h with pre/post reaches 730 sessions; 30m and 5m both return HTTP 422 for any range past 60 days. 34 release mornings at 30-minute resolution is therefore the ceiling this repo can build today, and what would raise it is a data source, not a better query. (4) A SECOND METHOD UPGRADE, EARNED BY A CASE WHERE THE FIRST ONE FAILS. The 09-28 sibling upgraded this chain's control from month-level to day>=22 because FHFA's last-Tuesday rule puts every release in the final third of its month. That control does NOT kill October: VIX9D/VIX on the five October release days is 1.0485 vs 0.9183, p=0.0148 against a day>=22 pool (0.0165 against all sessions, seed-stable 0.0157-0.0180). The driver is a REGIME, not a calendar day -- ALL FIVE October release days since 2021 sit inside an FOMC communications blackout, and blackout sessions as a class carry the steepening at 0.9884 vs 0.9065, p=0.0000 (n=408 vs 1,049). Controlled on blackout membership the release contributes nothing: release days in blackout vs OTHER blackout sessions p=0.2796, release days outside vs other clear sessions p=0.4533, October release days vs other late-October blackout sessions p=0.5579. The raw "release days in blackout vs out, p=0.0001" is entirely the Fed's. (5) WHICH THIRD OF THIS CALENDAR IS AFFECTED IS DETERMINISTIC. The last Tuesday falls inside a blackout in exactly four months -- January, April, July and OCTOBER -- 7 of 7 each across 2021-2027, and 0 of 7 in seven of the other eight (November 1 of 7). That is 22 of 67 post-policy releases, and it says which sibling ledgers need the blackout control (Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct) and which do not. (6) A SIBLING CLAIM IS NARROWED. The 2026-10-27 ledger read the FOMC day-one collision as structural. Day TWO is impossible -- 0 of 67 confirmed here from an independent parse -- but day ONE is month-specific: January and July collide 7 of 7 (arithmetic), April and October only 4 of 7 (2023, 2025, 2026, 2027 for October). 2027 happens to be a collision year, so this print IS FOMC day one, decision 2027-10-27, no SEP. The collision itself is null on everything: 16 of 67 releases on day one vs the other 51, smallest p 0.1093; vs other FOMC day-one sessions, smallest p 0.2287. A COUNT DISCREPANCY IS FLAGGED RATHER THAN RECONCILED: this session's parse of the same 271-row archive gives 67 releases and 16 day-one collisions where the 2026-10-27 ledger recorded 68 and 17. (7) CONTENT -- AUGUST IS THE SIXTH REFERENCE MONTH TESTED AND THE MOST ORDINARY. 13 of 14 positive since 2012 (median +0.4733%), 28 of 35 all-time (median +0.4002%), and it separates from the other eleven months at p=0.8982 all-time and p=0.9497 since 2012 -- the highest p-values this chain has recorded on a reference month, so August is null by a wide margin rather than by a near-miss. The live regime is flat (last six m/m 4 of 6 positive, median about +0.084%). IMPACT STAYS low. symbols: [] and 0 hits for any housing, house-price or macro keying in trade-playbooks.md or multi-symbol-sweep.md (re-grepped 2026-09-06); nothing here licenses an entry.
